title: Southern Live Oak: Ancient Live Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: The evergreen oak of the American South, mapped from a Dealey Plaza survivor of the JFK assassination to a champion growing in the Mojave desert.
intro: Southern live oak belongs to the humid coastal South, hung with Spanish moss and rarely far from salt air, which makes the mapped specimens here a study in the tree leaving home. One grows on a university mall in the Mojave desert, the state's largest recorded, ignoring every rule about its native range. Three stand in Dallas: two in Dealey Plaza, where the branches over Elm Street framed the shots fired at President Kennedy in 1963 and have stood over that ground ever since, and a stand of nineteen at Ferris Plaza that a mayor and a preservation coalition saved from removal in 1998 to keep a roost of grackles from being disturbed. None of these are the wild, low, shading giants of a Georgia churchyard. They are the species doing its ordinary trick, holding a canopy through drought and heat, in cities that happen to remember why it mattered.
